target_claim: There exists exactly one sequence of diagonal neighborhoods satisfying V_0 = V, symmetry of V_n for every n > 0, and V_n \circ V_n \subseteq V_{n-1} for every n > 0.
source_quote:
From [[Principle of Recursive Definition]], there exists [[Definition:Exactly One|exactly one]] [[Definition:Sequence|sequence]] $\sequence{V_n}_{n \in \N}$ of [[Definition:Neighborhood of Set|neighborhoods]] of the [[Definition:Diagonal Relation|diagonal $\Delta_X$]] in $\struct {X \times X, \tau_{X \times X} }$:
:$V_0 = V$
:$\forall n \in \N_{> 0} : V_n$ is [[Definition:Symmetric Relation|symmetric]] as a [[Definition:Relation as Subset of Cartesian Product|relation]] on $X \times X$
:$\forall n \in \N_{> 0}$ the [[Definition:Composite Relation|composite relation]] $V_n \circ V_n$ is a [[Definition:Subset|subset]] of $V_{n - 1}$, that is, $V_n \circ V_n \subseteq V_{n - 1}$
